title: RCMP officer cleared of wrongdoing in July 2012 fatal shooting
article: The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) has released its ruling in a shooting dating back to mid-July 2012 near Vegreville that left one man dead.
The investigation stemmed from an alleged domestic dispute in a rural area near Vegreville - officers from the Vegreville and Two Hills RCMP detachments were called to the home.

It was reported that the dispute had escalated between a man and members of his family - while RCMP were on their way to the home, another call came in, reporting the man had a shotgun outside the home, while family members were inside.
As a result, an RCMP crisis negotiator and members from the RCMP Emergency Response Team were requested - and the officers on the scene tried to get the armed man to put down his firearm.
However, the man wouldn't follow directions - and eventually started to approach one of the officers while still armed.
ASIRT said that officer fired one shot at the man, wounding him - while the officers on the scene tried to administer first aid, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.
Investigators with ASIRT announced Wednesday that the officer responded properly in that situation, and charges would not be laid.
